_comment: Endpoint presets. Each entry is both a per-endpoint quirk table for the OpenAI-compatible client (matched by base_url) and a starting point the dashboard offers when adding an endpoint: picking one fills in the URL, the protocol and the key variable, and carries the quirks the endpoint needs. An endpoint with no entry here gets the portable default: bare model name, no extra headers, no reasoning remap. Add or override entries with MIRA_PROVIDERS_JSON_PATH.

_fields.label: Display name, shown on the Connections page and under each model picker.
_fields.description: One sentence for the card and the preset list.
_fields.docs_url: Where the provider documents its API and plans.
_fields._naming: An entry's key is what `llm.provider` names it by, so it may not be 'openai' or 'bedrock': those two have always meant the generic OpenAI-compatible backend and AWS Bedrock, and an entry taking either name would be unreachable from the config file. OpenAI's own API is therefore 'openai-api'.
_fields.base_url: The endpoint this profile applies to; `llm.base_url` is matched against it, and the dashboard prefills it. `llm.provider: <name>` fills it in too.
_fields.api_key_env: Environment variable holding the key when one is not stored in Mira's database. "" means the endpoint needs no key.
_fields.api_style: Protocol dialect the endpoint is reached with: 'chat' (Chat Completions) or 'responses'.
_fields.model_prefix: 'keep' sends the full vendor/model id (OpenRouter routes on it); 'strip' sends the bare model name.
_fields.extra_headers: Headers added to every request (attribution, client identification).
_fields.reasoning_effort_map: Renames for the unified reasoning.effort levels this endpoint spells differently.
_fields.session_header: Optional header carrying a stable per-conversation id (one per client instance, so one per review pass), for endpoints that route and cache by it.
_fields.usage_url: Optional GET endpoint reporting the key's allowance. Its document is read by the parser named in usage_format.
_fields.usage_format: Which parser reads usage_url's document (see mira.llm.key_providers). Currently: 'opencode-go'.
